the production of when- questions in L1 acquisition is delayed because of the cognitive factors that are related to the bound variable reading, and that the production of these questions in L2 acquisition is also delayed due to the internal linguistic factor of the complexity of the bound variable reading.

the acquisition of when-questions by English-speaking children, both native and non-native.

children's production of when- questions in L1 acquisition is delayed due to a combination of cognitive and linguistic factors.
children produce when-questions when they understand the bound variable reading of tense.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
when-questions appear late because they are complex.
the late production of when- questions is due to the fact that children have not learned to understand bound variables.
the delayed acquisition of wh-questions is a result of the interaction of cognitive and internal linguistic factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the internal linguistic factors that are responsible for the delayed production of the when-question in L1 acquisition also play a role in L2 acquisition.

internal factors, such as the interaction between the interrogative when and the bound variable tense, can explain the late appearance of wh-questions in L2 children who have already mastered bound variable readings in L1.
when-questions provide evidence for the acquisition of the bound variable reading of tense, which is a crucial component of the grammar of natural language.
